title: Overlapping Brasileirao files double-counted: standings/stats inflated ~2x
evidence: soccer_mcp.py:85-105 loads Brasileirao_Matches.csv AND novo_campeonato_brasileiro.csv both under competition 'Brasileirao' with no dedup (2019 has 380 rows in each = 760). Runtime check: standings(2019) reports Flamengo-RJ played=76 pts=180 vs correct 38/90; the 'Brasileirao' bucket holds 11066 matches = 4180+6886.
suggestion: Deduplicate overlapping seasons across Brasileirao_Matches.csv and novo_campeonato_brasileiro.csv (e.g. skip novo rows whose season is covered by the primary file, or key matches by date+teams) before aggregating standings/stats.

title: MCP tools advertise empty inputSchema {"type":"object"} with no properties
evidence: soccer_mcp.py:241 emits inputSchema {"type": "object"} for all 7 tools. Verified via tools/list: 7 tools returned, first inputSchema = {'type':'object'}. A schema-driven LLM client cannot discover argument names (team, season, competition, ...).
suggestion: Add per-tool properties/required to each inputSchema so clients know how to call the tools; R1's server + tool definitions otherwise exist and dispatch correctly (main() soccer_mcp.py:235-248).

title: Factual gate scored 0.0: no tool returned a correct 2019 Serie A table naming Flamengo
evidence: _factual.json: {ok:false, score:0.0, note:'no tool returned a 2019 Serie A table naming Flamengo'}. standings(2019) does name Flamengo-RJ but the row is double-counted (76 played/180 pts), and the table is keyed under competition 'Brasileirao' not 'Serie A'. Root cause is the R9 double-count plus competition-label mismatch.
suggestion: Fix the R9 dedup so standings(2019) yields Flamengo 90 pts / 38 played; consider aliasing 'Serie A' -> 'Brasileirao'.
